title: Prysmian Group
excerpt: Most operators overlook how Prysmian Group drives unit economics and competitive moats at scale. Understanding its real-world mechanics reveals why.
author: Sofia Rossi

body.text: Most operators overlook how Prysmian Group drives unit economics and competitive moats at scale. Understanding its real-world mechanics reveals why disciplined organizations outperform during market shifts.

is a multinational company with headquarters in Bicocca, Milan, Italy, specializing in the production, installation and maintenance of electrical cables and optical cables for digital connections. Prysmian is present all over the world with 109 plants, 29 in North America, 13 in LATAM, 50 in EMEA.
Prysmian was formerly part of Pirelli. It was spun off in 2005 as a stand-alone company, and listed in 2007.

It is the world's largest cable manufacturer and a global leader in the energy and telecommunications cable industry. The company is listed on the Borsa Italiana in the FTSE MIB index, with a market capitalisation of approximately €42 billion as of May 2026.
On 4 December 2017, it took over 100% of the General Cable group in the US, to then complete the merger by incorporation the following year.
History
The beginning
The company originated in 1879 as Pirelli Cavi e Sistemi. In 1881, it secured a contract to produce submarine telegraph cables for military engineering.

In 1886, it opened a submarine cable production plant in La Spezia. It later helped to lay the entire Italian telegraph network on behalf of the Italian state-owned company Telegrafi dello Stato, and to install the electrical grid for domestic use in Milan. It also laid telegraph cables in the colonies of Italian East Africa.

In 1925, it produced 5,150 km of submarine telegraph cabling for Italcable for communications between Italy and South America. Its collaboration with the Italian government continued with the laying of cables for the Italian interurban telephone network.
Prysmian

was created by Goldman Sachs after acquiring Pirelli & C. A's Cables and Systems business. After restructuring the organisation of the group's internal activities, the company decided to sell down its investment in the cable market.

3 billion: Goldman Sachs gave Pirelli 225 million and the rest (more than one billion) was a debt that would be paid off the back of the new business. The company, led by Valerio Battista from 2005, was then a public company.
Since 3 May 2007, it has been listed on the Milan Stock Exchange and on 24 September 2007 it joined the S&P MIB index of the biggest Italian companies.
At the end of 2009, Goldman Sachs decided to sell down its stake, which was completed in March 2010.

In February 2011, Prysmian successfully made a takeover bid of EUR 840 million for Dutch company Draka, with headquarters in Eindhoven, which at the time was fourth in the world in the cable and optical fibre sector.
The combination expanded the group's operations to over 50 countries and integrated Draka's portfolio across the power, telecommunications, industrial, and submarine cable sectors.
In December 2017, it bought the American (and rival) company General Cable based in Kentucky. 5 billion) and financial debt.

This merged the leading cable-making company in the world in terms of revenue (Prysmian) and the fourth (General Cable), creating a group with a revenue of EUR 10 billion, EBIDTA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation) of EUR 840 million and over 28,000 employees.

The transaction was completed in June 2018, expanding the group’s manufacturing capacity for copper, aluminium, and fibre optic wire and cable products across the energy, communications, industrial, and construction sectors.
Acquisition of General Cable
The General Cable group was valued at 3 billion dollars with a price premium of approximately 81% to General Cable's share value on the last day of trading.

The acquisition was unanimously approved by the two Boards of Directors and would create a company in 50 countries with 31,000 employees, which could generate revenue of 11 billion dollars a year, based on estimates from the 2017 financial statements. The integration was expected to cost 220 million dollars.

The price per share paid to General Cable was 30 dollars, versus a Prysmian dividend that was halved in 2011 after the acquisition of Draka, and stable at 43 cents per share. The General Cable group has one billion dollars of debt.

Already the leading cable company in the world, with such "pro-forma" earnings, it would become twice as large as its second main competitor. Prysmian declared that it expects to increase its capital by more than 500 million in light of further acquisitions.
The transaction was subject to approval by the antitrust authorities of the two countries.

Its completion would create a market concentration in a strategic sector for public safety and economic development, which was already established by no more than ten competitors across Italy, the US and China. Other oligopolies exist in the fixed and mobile telephony sectors in various countries, partly due to the existence of natural monopolies.
M&A and expansion (2024-present)

In 2024, Prysmian acquired Warren & Brown, an Australian manufacturer of telecommunication network connectivity products, specializing in Fiber-to-the-Antenna (FTTA), Fiber-to-the-Home (FTTH), and data centre applications. Founded in 1921 and headquartered in Melbourne, the company operates three main production facilities, two located in Melbourne, Australia, and one in Manila, Philippines.

The operation aimed to utilize cross-selling opportunities and operational efficiencies by integrating Encore Wire’s production, distribution processes, and service levels.
The combined business was structured to support electrification and digital transformation projects in North America, specifically targeting the expansion of data centres and power grid upgrades.

Prysmian finalized the acquisition of Channell Commercial Corporation in June 2025 for a base purchase price of $950 million, subject to customary adjustments. Based in the United States, Channell Commercial Corporation is a manufacturer of thermoplastic enclosures and fibre management solutions.

The transaction was designed to expand the Prysmian’s North American portfolio by integrating its existing optical cable products with Channell’s infrastructure components. The integration aimed to provide end-to-end Fiber-to-the-Home services. Beyond FTTH, the acquisition was structured to support the roll-out of 5G networks and the expansion of data centres.

The group’s expansion continued in December 2025 through a Fincantieri-partnered joint venture to acquire Xtera Topco Limited, a provider of turnkey submarine telecommunications systems based in the UK and the US. The operation expanded the group’s presence in the global submarine telecommunications market.

Headquartered in London, Xtera is identified as one of five companies capable of delivering subsea telecommunications networks on a global scale. The acquisition aimed to leverage the company’s management structure and its track record in project delivery within the submarine telecommunications sector.
The transaction was completed on 13 October 2026, through a joint venture owned by Prysmian (80%) and Fincantieri (20%).
In February 2026, Prysmian completed the acquisition of the Spanish company ACSM for a transaction value of €169 million.

The operation aimed at incorporating the entire lifecycle of subsea assets within the group’s services, including activities ranging from pre-installation and preparation to installation and protection, as well as post-installation activities such as inspection, maintenance, and repair, and eventual decommissioning of underwater infrastructure.

The acquisition was designed to expand Prysmian’s North American product portfolio through the addition of cable-adjacent infrastructure products, including conduit and cable management systems targeting the electrification, power grid, data centre, and artificial intelligence infrastructure sectors.

Activity

The company is the global leader in the cable systems sector. Specifically, Prysmian produces and lays underground and submarine cables for the transmission and distribution of electricity, as well as specialised cables for use in various industrial contexts, and medium- and low-voltage cables for construction and infrastructure.
For telecoms, the Group produces copper cables, optical cables and optical fibre for the transmission of data, video and voice. Prysmian is the world’s largest buyer of copper as a single company.
On the customer's request, Prysmian also designs and produces key systems and takes care of post-installation maintenance.

Every year, Prysmian invests more than EUR 100 million in research and development. This has allowed the Group to develop innovations like BendBrightXS 160μm, the narrowest bend-insensitive optical fibre, and FlexRibbon, which, with 6,912 fibres, is the optical cable with the highest number of fibres in the sector.
